label: sparse copy-phase feature on early-recall inputs n/x/l/c/0 (unexplained selectivity)
explanation: Fires almost only in the copy phase (93% of mass), mostly at recall_idx 1-4 (peaks at 1 and 3), and almost only when the fed-back input is n, x, l, c or 0 (n alone is 30% of mass). The strongest examples are sequences starting n l ..., where it fires on the n right after <DEL>; the output being l (as in n->l) also goes with stronger firing. It is nearly silent in the original phase, at t<3, and at late recall positions. But only about 1% of steps matching (copy phase, input in {n,x,l,c,0}, recall_idx<=4) actually fire. No condition we tried on prev_tok, out_tok, next_out, recall position or first token pushed precision above about 4% without losing most of the recall. So which of these steps fire seems to depend on sequence context that the per-step variables do not capture. The predicate gets about 80% recall and mass recall but F1 of only about 0.03.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=7: n, x, l, c; t=6: n, x, l, c; t=8: n, x, l, c) and the token being output, by phase (delimiter step: s, n, 0, x; copy phase: l, s, i, n; input phase: ); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=4, L=4 & t=5, recall_idx=3.
